lead_headline: Restaurant tracker adds 3 new leads today as foreclosures deliver zero $4M+ filings and subscriber count flatlines for third consecutive day

restaurant.blurb: 3 new leads today push active count to 94 (49 openings, 45 closures)—Thursday additions: Maize by Chef Johnny Curiel preps Michelin-starred RiNo opening in Globeville, Taco John's Globeville location flags opening uncertainty, Peg and Willy's Shave Ice truck shutters Stapleton operations.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications today extend statewide freeze to 40 consecutive days—Thursday marks tenth straight zero-filing session as April's first nine days post 0/10 shutout, now surpassing December 2024's 12-day record by 233%. System blackout enters sixth week with no Liquor Enforcement Division updates across all Colorado counties (Denver, Arapahoe, Douglas, Jefferson, Adams) and all license types (retail, tavern, hotel/restaurant, brew pub). Estimated backlog climbs to 90-120 applications as void obliterates January-February's 15-20 weekly baseline—database holds 13,731 historical entries but registers zero March 1–April 9 activity.

reputation.blurb: 4 mentions yesterday lift week to 46 citations (−30% vs prior week's 66) across 15 sources—Wednesday's quartet led by Denver Post Leprino Foods lawsuit coverage and Business Journals Arizona startup piece. Week's leaders: Instagram (17 mentions), Denver Post (6), Facebook (6), with social platforms claiming 59% share versus traditional media's 41% split. Daily mention rate slides to 6.6/day from last week's 9.4/day, confirming April's sustained decline after March's 10+/day baseline. Source diversity holds at 15 outlets but pickup velocity continues downward trajectory through mid-week.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +0 yesterday (0 new, 0 canceled) marks third consecutive flatline day as MTD slips to −1 (−0.1/day through 9 days) while 90-day net holds +137. Past week delivers −2 net (6 new, 8 canceled) versus prior week's +10 (27 new, 17 canceled), marking 120% reversal as acquisition craters 78% while cancellations decline 53%. Nine-day April start posts −1 net (15 new, 16 canceled) versus March's opening stretch (+29 net), confirming 103% momentum flip. Recent pattern splits sharply: late March surged +18 net (+2.6/day), early April stumbled −19 net (−2.4/day)—current three-day freeze suggests stabilization after churn spike but trails YTD +1.3/day pace by 108%.
